cards.name: Forage
cards.flavor: When the stores run thin, the young go out at dawn and come back with roots, nuts and the odd unlucky hare.

cards.name: Anarchy
cards.flavor: When the old order breaks, no one rules and everyone does: granaries are thrown open, debts are burned, and whoever shouts loudest in the square decides each day anew.

quote.text: Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold; mere anarchy is loosed upon the world.
quote.by: W. B. Yeats, The Second Coming

cards.text: 1 action each turn. Only order cards can be played; nothing can be grown, bought or researched. Each turn it eats 20% of stored food and wealth. Lasts up to 4 turns, fewer the calmer the people; calming shortens it. From its second turn, buy order for 2, 6, 12 or 20 wealth with 1–4 turns left. When it ends, choose a government from your government deck. Each turn: trash 1 card, +1 per turn so far, from your hand, deck or discard (−1 unrest each).

cards.name: Egypt
cards.flavor: Along a thin green ribbon of the Nile, the yearly flood laid down black silt, and pharaohs raised monuments meant to outlast time.

quote.text: Egypt is the gift of the river.

cards.name: Sumer
cards.flavor: Between the Tigris and the Euphrates, the Sumerians dug canals, built the first cities, and pressed wedges into clay to keep their accounts: the first writing.

quote.text: Go up on the wall of Uruk and walk around.

cards.name: Phoenicia
cards.flavor: From Tyre and Sidon, Phoenician ships carried cedar, glass and purple dye across the Mediterranean, and their alphabet travelled with them.

quote.text: A merchant of the people for many isles.

cards.name: Babylon
cards.flavor: Hammurabi carved his laws in stone for all to see, and Babylon's astronomers kept the most careful records of the heavens in the ancient world.

quote.text: That the strong should not harm the weak.

cards.name: Greece
cards.flavor: Rival city-states argued in the agora, staged tragedies in open theatres, and asked questions philosophers still ask.

quote.text: The unexamined life is not worth living.

cards.name: Persia
cards.flavor: Cyrus and Darius ruled the largest empire yet seen, held together by satraps, respect for local customs, and a road of relay stations from Sardis to Susa.

quote.text: Neither snow nor rain nor heat nor gloom of night stays these couriers from the swift completion of their appointed rounds.

cards.name: Harvest Festival
cards.flavor: The last sheaf is cut and carried home with songs; for one night the whole village eats as if winter will never come.

cards.name: Envoys from the Hills
cards.flavor: Hill chieftains arrive with gifts of furs and honey, and they expect gifts in return.

cards.name: Plague
cards.flavor: A fever comes up the river with the boats; the healers burn herbs, and the gravediggers never rest.

cards.name: Granary Fire
cards.flavor: A lamp tips over in the night, and by dawn a season's grain is ash and smoke.

cards.name: Drought
cards.flavor: No rain since the spring sowing; the plains crack, and the herds walk farther each day to drink.

cards.name: Silt Flood
cards.flavor: The river rises over its banks and leaves behind a gift of black mud, thick and rich.

cards.name: Bumper Harvest
cards.flavor: The ears hang so heavy the stalks bend, and every barn in the land is full to the rafters.

cards.name: Busy Harbours
cards.flavor: Sails crowd every bay, and the quays ring with tongues from across the sea.

cards.name: Visiting Scholar
cards.flavor: A stranger who reads the stars and counts in strange numerals asks only for a roof and a lamp.

cards.name: Labour Shortage
cards.flavor: The young men have gone to the mines and the boats, and the fields wait for hands that do not come.

cards.name: Tax Revolt
cards.flavor: The tax collectors come back empty-handed and bloodied; the villages say they have paid enough.

cards.name: Wandering Smiths
cards.flavor: Smiths from the far hills set up their forge by the gate and offer to teach their secrets, for a price.

cards.name: Pestilence
cards.flavor: The sickness spreads through the crowded streets faster than the priests can name it.

cards.name: Library Burns
cards.flavor: The scrolls catch like dry grass, and a hundred years of learning rises into the night sky.

cards.name: Debased Coin
cards.flavor: The mint cuts the silver with lead, and soon the merchants weigh every coin twice and trust none.

cards.name: Storm at Sea
cards.flavor: Three days of gales, and the harbours fill with wreckage instead of cargo.

cards.name: Golden Age
cards.flavor: Peace, full granaries and clever hands: for a few bright years, everything the realm attempts succeeds.

cards.name: School of Philosophers
cards.flavor: Under the plane trees, old men argue about the nature of things, and their students write it all down.

cards.name: Succession Crisis
cards.flavor: The old ruler dies with three heirs and no will, and each one has friends with swords.

cards.name: Mercenaries' Offer
cards.flavor: Hard men with foreign shields wait at the gate; they will fight for anyone who pays in silver.

cards.name: Solstice Rites
cards.flavor: On the longest night, fires burn on every hill and the elders watch for the sun to turn back.

cards.name: Traveling Bards
cards.flavor: Strangers with lyres trade songs of far-off kings for a meal and a place by the fire.

cards.name: Comet Sighted
cards.flavor: A long-haired star hangs over the fields for weeks, and the priests argue whether it foretells a birth or a death.

cards.name: Distant Drums
cards.flavor: From beyond the hills, drums beat through the night. No one has seen the drummers yet.

cards.name: Wild Berries
cards.flavor: The hedges hang heavy with fruit this year, and the children come home with purple hands.

cards.name: Wandering Trader
cards.flavor: A lone trader leads a laden donkey into the square, with salt, beads and news from the coast.

cards.name: Local Legend
cards.flavor: A shepherd who wrestled a lion becomes a hero; by the third retelling, it was two lions.

cards.name: Mild Spring
cards.flavor: The thaw comes early and gentle, and the rivers rise just enough.

cards.name: Famine
cards.flavor: The granaries echo. Families eat the seed grain, then the oxen, and pray for the next harvest.
cards.text: Each hungry upkeep: +1 counter (max 3), −1 pop (largest territory) and +1 unrest per counter. Ends when your pop is fed.

cards.name: Market Day
cards.flavor: The square fills with stalls, haggling and gossip, and coins change hands faster than rumours.

cards.name: Good Omens
cards.flavor: An eagle circles the citadel three times, and the augurs declare the gods well pleased.

cards.name: Grumbling
cards.flavor: At the wells and in the taverns, people mutter about taxes, the harvest and the ones who rule them.

cards.name: Omen of Doom
cards.flavor: A calf is born with two heads and the moon turns red; the soothsayers will not meet anyone's eye.

cards.name: Bandit Raids
cards.flavor: Masked riders strike the roads at dusk, and caravans arrive late, light, or not at all.

cards.name: Raiders
cards.flavor: Dust on the horizon: riders from the steppe, come for the harvest.

cards.name: Sea Raiders
cards.flavor: Long ships are beached in the night, and the harbour stores are their prize.

cards.name: Hill Tribes
cards.flavor: The clans of the high valleys come down when their own stores run thin.

cards.name: Calls for Reform
cards.flavor: Petitioners crowd the palace steps, demanding fairer laws and a say in how they are made.

cards.name: Peasant Uprising
cards.flavor: Pitchforks and torches: the farmers have had enough, and the steward's house burns first.

cards.name: Radical Thinkers
cards.flavor: Teachers in the agora question the gods, the laws and the king, and the young listen.

cards.name: Pottery
cards.flavor: Fired clay holds grain, water and oil through the seasons, and broken sherds still tell us who lived where.

quote.text: Who is the Potter, pray, and who the Pot?
quote.by: Rubáiyát of Omar Khayyám, tr. Edward FitzGerald

cards.name: Animal Husbandry
cards.flavor: Wild aurochs, goats and sheep become herds: milk, wool, hides and patient strength for the plough.

quote.text: The master's eye fattens the horse.

cards.name: Irrigation
cards.flavor: Canals and ditches lead river water out to thirsty fields, and the desert's edge turns green.

quote.text: Egypt is the gift of the river.

cards.name: The Plough
cards.flavor: Yoked oxen drag a wooden share through heavy soil, and one family can sow fields that once took a village.

quote.text: He that by the plough would thrive, himself must either hold or drive.

cards.name: Weaving
cards.flavor: Flax and wool spun and woven on upright looms make cloth, the greatest trade of the ancient world after bread.

quote.text: She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.

cards.name: Clay Tokens
cards.flavor: Little clay cones, spheres and discs stand for sheep and measures of grain, sealed in envelopes as a receipt.

quote.text: God made the integers; all else is the work of man.

cards.name: Fermentation
cards.flavor: Grain left wet in a jar turns to beer: it keeps for months, and Sumerian workers draw their wages in it.

quote.text: And wine that maketh glad the heart of man.

cards.name: Mining
cards.flavor: Copper, tin and flint are dug from the hills in narrow shafts lit by oil lamps.

quote.text: Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it.

cards.name: Mysticism
cards.flavor: Shamans and seers read meaning in stars, dreams and entrails, and the first shrines rise.

quote.text: There are more things in heaven and earth, Horatio, than are dreamt of in your philosophy.

cards.name: The Wheel
cards.flavor: First spun by potters in Mesopotamia, the wheel soon carries carts, chariots and trade across the plains.

quote.text: As it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel.

cards.name: Masonry
cards.flavor: Cut stone, fitted tight, raises walls, tombs and temples meant to stand forever.

quote.text: I found Rome a city of bricks and left it a city of marble.
quote.by: Augustus, in Suetonius' Lives of the Caesars

cards.name: Bronze Working
cards.flavor: Copper alloyed with tin makes harder blades and tools, and a hunger for tin that sends traders across the seas.

quote.text: Their armour was of bronze, and their houses of bronze, and of bronze were their implements.

cards.name: Writing
cards.flavor: Marks pressed into clay to count grain grow into a way to keep laws, letters and epics.

quote.text: The written word remains.

cards.name: Weights and Measures
cards.flavor: Silver weighed out in shekels and grain in fixed measures let strangers trade without haggling over every sack.

quote.text: A false balance is abomination to the Lord: but a just weight is his delight.

cards.name: Olive and Vine
cards.flavor: Olive trees and vines take years to bear, then bear for lifetimes; their oil and wine sail out in amphorae.

quote.text: A land of wheat, and barley, and vines, and fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of oil olive, and honey.

cards.name: Medicine
cards.flavor: In Egypt's Houses of Life, priest-physicians copy papyri on wounds, fevers and remedies, and tend the sick.

quote.text: Life is short, the art long.

cards.name: Credit
cards.flavor: Temple and palace lend silver and barley at interest on clay contracts, and debtors who cannot repay are sold.

quote.text: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.

cards.name: Sailing
cards.flavor: Reed boats, then planked hulls under square sails, carry cargo, colonists and ideas along the coasts.

quote.text: To sail is necessary; to live is not.
quote.by: Pompey, in Plutarch's Life of Pompey

cards.name: Priesthood
cards.flavor: A class of priests keeps the temples, the rites and the granaries, and speaks to kings for the gods.

quote.text: Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.

cards.name: Code of Laws
cards.flavor: Written laws, set in stone for all to read, replace the whim of the chief with fixed rules.

quote.text: Let the good of the people be the supreme law.

cards.name: Calendar
cards.flavor: Watching the Nile's flood and the rising of Sirius, the Egyptians count a year of 365 days.

quote.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.

cards.name: Philosophy
cards.flavor: Greek thinkers ask what the world is made of and how one should live, and answer with reason, not myth.

quote.text: Philosophy begins in wonder.

cards.name: Iron Working
cards.flavor: Iron is harder to smelt than bronze, but its ore is everywhere: soon every farmer has an iron blade.

quote.text: For now truly is a race of iron, and men never rest from labour and sorrow by day.

cards.name: Mathematics
cards.flavor: Babylonian tables, Egyptian surveyors and Greek geometers turn counting into proof.

quote.text: There is no royal road to geometry.
quote.by: Euclid to Ptolemy I, in Proclus

cards.name: Coinage
cards.flavor: Lydian kings stamp lumps of electrum with a lion's head, and a coin's worth no longer needs a balance.

quote.text: The Lydians were the first men whom we know who coined and used gold and silver currency.

cards.name: Bureaucracy
cards.flavor: Satraps govern the provinces, scribes keep the tax rolls, and royal couriers ride the roads between them.

quote.text: Neither snow nor rain nor heat nor gloom of night stays these couriers from the swift completion of their appointed rounds.

cards.name: Alphabet
cards.flavor: Phoenician traders cut hundreds of signs down to 22 letters, and reading is no longer for scribes alone.

quote.text: In the beginning was the Word.

cards.name: Qanat
cards.flavor: Persian diggers tunnel gently downhill from a mountain's water table, and fields grow green in the desert.

quote.text: For in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.

cards.name: Navigation
cards.flavor: Steering by the stars, Phoenician ships leave the coast behind and cross open sea to Carthage and Gades.

quote.text: They that go down to the sea in ships, that do business in great waters.

cards.name: Astronomy
cards.flavor: Priests atop the ziggurats chart the wandering stars and learn to foretell eclipses.

quote.text: The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.

cards.name: Engineering
cards.flavor: Arches, aqueducts and roads carry water and armies across whole provinces.

quote.text: Give me a place to stand, and I will move the earth.
